endorsements.quote: Adaptive platform trials offer a scalable framework for continuous, comparative, equity-focused evaluation by testing multiple AI tools and updates head-to-head within a master protocol that standardizes populations, endpoints, decision rules, and governance, while allowing dynamic addition or removal of arms and reuse of control groups.

unlisted_practices: Use adaptive platform trials with a master protocol to evaluate multiple clinical AI tools and their updated versions head-to-head without restarting a new trial each time.
Prespecify the minimum concurrent-control sample size that must be met under a new comparator before further graduation decisions in platform trials.
Base primary inference in clinical AI platform trials on concurrent controls, with any borrowing of non-concurrent control data prespecified and supported by sensitivity analyses.
Establish independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board oversight and a multidisciplinary steering committee for clinical AI platform trials.
Perform AI version upgrades and arm discontinuations in trials only at prespecified interim boundaries, with defined retraining periods and parallel run-in phases where feasible.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/framework article arguing for adaptive platform trials as a clinical trial methodology and governance approach to modernize evidence generation for clinical AI.
